source: integrations/core/test/intent.test.mjs (the sentences its tests give to detection)
notes: Every sentence the plugin intent tests give to forget detection, with what detectForgetRequests(text, {previous}) returns. requests: the forget requests in order, each {statement (the words sent to /memory/forget/prepare, before secret redaction), inChat, ownTurn}; [] means the sentence asks nothing. statement and inChat repeat the first request (null when none). inChat true: the service's in-chat check reads the same request with the same statement today. inChat false: only the plugin reads it, or reads fewer words (a cut replacement). A service that mirrors the plugin reads every inChat-false request with the same statement and none of the [] sentences. The rules are conservative: a false request deletes the user's data without a word, a missed one is said again more plainly. So complaints, questions, recall requests and instructions about code, files or apps are [] even where the service reads them today, for example "Don't remember my address." and "Never remember my address." (a bare noun phrase without please: often the user's own "(I) don't remember …"), 忘记我的密码了 and 你忘了我的生日吧 ("(I/you) forgot …"), 别记错我的生日 and 把我的分支删掉. A statement shorter than the request's object (a cut) keeps a new value out of what is forgotten only when it is the last clause, restates an address, a name, a number or an email, and says nothing more ("Forget my old address, I live at 27 Birch Lane now."); any other clause stays in the statement: a missed cut is safe, a wrong one is not.
